clue.text: Insignificant tyrant captured by nationalist rulers, according to reports

indicators.note: something captured by another is held inside it, so the tyrant sits within the nationalist

parts.note: an ogre is a cruel, tyrannical figure

indicators.note: reports are things heard, so the rulers' word is given by its sound

parts.note: sheikhs are Arab rulers

explanation.surface: A minor despot is seized by nationalist leaders, so the news says.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone covers only the rulers: sheikhs is often said to rhyme with shakes. 'captured by' and 'according to reports' are the two signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for something unremarkable or mediocre, describing anything of little importance.

clue.text: Series of battles giving northern Salonica power after a struggle

indicators.note: after a struggle the letters are thrown about and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A war history describing how northern Salonica gained power after fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a struggle' scrambles the place name and the power word together; 'giving' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The campaigns fought by France under its emperor from 1803 to 1815 were a long series of battles.

clue.text: Reach over the top, say, stretching upwards

indicators.note: in a down entry, stretching upwards means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: OTT is the abbreviation for over the top, meaning excessive
say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: Someone reaches over the top of something, stretching up to do it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretching upwards' turns both pieces round as one run, which only works because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive at a place is to reach it, a common phrasal verb.

clue.text: With both hands clean, dine out in part of London

indicators.note: out here means on the outside, so the dining word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: to dine is to eat
R and L stand for right and left, the two hands
to scour is to scrub clean

explanation.surface: Advice to wash both hands before going out to dinner in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' puts EAT outside RL + SCOUR. EARLS COURT is a district of west London, once home to a big exhibition centre.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a named district in west London, so it fits as one part of the city.

clue.text: Criticised female engaged in business out east

indicators.note: engaged in means taking part within, so the female sits inside the business word
out means removed, so the east letter is dropped from the business word

parts.note: trade is commerce or business
E is the compass abbreviation for east
she is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman working in a trade in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops the east letter, leaving TRAD; 'engaged in' then puts the female inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashed is slang for harshly criticised or panned, as a critic does to a bad show.

clue.text: Imposing abode queen's in charge of

parts.note: an abode is a home
R is short for regina, the Latin word for queen

explanation.surface: A grand house where a queen is the person in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic and heroic in scale, like the poems of ancient Greece, and so grand or imposing.

clue.text: King and ace turned over in game of chance

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the ace word is read backwards

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: Playing cards are flipped over in a gambling game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' turns ONE into ENO.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery-style gambling game in which players bet on drawn numbers, so purely chance.

clue.text: Old City team reduced by two after match day becomes gloomy

indicators.note: after means the city and team pieces follow the match day in the answer

parts.note: Saturday, SAT, is the traditional day for football matches in Britain
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia
a football team is eleven, and two fewer is nine

explanation.surface: A city football side, down to nine men after a Saturday match, are downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain football is traditionally played on Saturday, so 'match day' gives SAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a sullen or gloomy temperament, as people born under Saturn supposedly have.

clue.text: Gent had popped into mobile library first thing

indicators.note: mobile means moving about, so the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A gentleman visited the travelling library early in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' rearranges GENT HAD and LIBRARY, with 'popped into' only joining them, though it also looks like a library van call.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe early morning, the time when one is up and about at the start of the day.

clue.text: In pop, girl's taken to Queen

parts.note: Pat is a girl's name
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A girl takes a liking to the Queen in pop music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' looks like music but is a word for father.
explanation.definitionFit: Pater is a dated Latin-derived word for father, and pop is an informal one.

clue.text: One who censures commercial television

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an ad
a monitor is a screen like a television set

explanation.surface: A critic who rails against TV advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: An admonitor is someone who admonishes, that is, reproves or censures another.

clue.text: Principal part in new version of Hair, no less

indicators.note: a new version of something reworks it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lead role in a revival of the musical Hair, no less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new version of' rearranges HAIR and NO LESS. Hair is a rock musical of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for the largest portion of something, the bulk or main part.

clue.text: Bind wound finally with piece of material

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: Dressing a wound with a strip of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bind' looks like tying a bandage, but it is the noun: a bore or nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a bind and a drag are both a tedious, annoying chore.

clue.text: Formally attired, English soldiers capture South American capital

indicators.note: attired means dressed, so the pieces go inside the garment

parts.note: a gown is formal dress, worn by someone dressed formally
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
to get is to capture or seize

explanation.surface: English troops, dressed formally, take a South American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attired' is the container signal: soldiers dressed in formal wear are inside the gown.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Guyana, on the north coast of South America.

clue.text: Not by the way food RAF distributed

indicators.note: food distributed is spread around, so its letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Food parcels dropped by the RAF in a place with no roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges FOOD and RAF. 'way' here means road.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-road means away from roads or tracks, and a way is a road.

clue.text: Wicked fighters thrown into cooler with verbal threat of punishment

indicators.note: thrown into means put inside, so the fighters go into the middle of the rest

parts.note: a fan cools you

indicators.note: verbal means spoken, so only the sound of the threat word counts

parts.note: the stick, as in carrot and stick, is a threat of punishment
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are thrown in the cooler and threatened with a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verbal' gives STIC, said exactly like the threat word; 'thrown into' puts the fighters inside. 'Wicked' is slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, wicked means excellent, the same praise as calling something superb.

clue.text: Box containing a thousand and one drugs supplied by me?

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the box wraps the other letters

parts.note: a chest is a box
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A box holding a thousand and one medicines.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the answer: who supplies drugs?
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist dispenses medicines, so the question asks who supplies them.

clue.text: Gold pinched by foreigner without warning? I'll turn a blind eye

indicators.note: pinched by means gripped inside, so the gold sits within the other piece
without means lacking, so the warning is taken away from foreigner

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Gold stolen by a foreigner without notice; I'll look the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' leaves IGNER; 'pinched by' puts the gold inside it. The question mark marks the definition as a self-description.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who turns a blind eye pays no attention, which is what one who disregards does.

clue.text: Drinks bought at university gathering

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for the group
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Students buy drinks at a university get-together.
explanation.definitionFit: A round-up is an assembly or collecting together, of cattle or people.

clue.text: Swelling in an advanced state? You might need me

parts.note: a surge is a swelling, as of the sea
on means advanced, as when the night is well on

explanation.surface: A patient's swelling has got worse, and a doctor speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the answer: someone a bad swelling might send you to.
explanation.definitionFit: An operating doctor is who a patient with a worsening swelling might need.

clue.text: Guess how many parts in The Entertainer

indicators.note: parts in means the answer is made of parts of the words, running across them

explanation.surface: A quiz asking how many roles there are in the play The Entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Entertainer is a play by John Osborne, but here it is just a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A showman is a performer or impresario who puts on entertainment.

clue.text: Attention given to women's clothes

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
an ear means attention, as in lend an ear

explanation.surface: Notice paid to what women are wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Wear means garments, as in evening wear or menswear.

clue.text: Lively music highly unsuitable at first, on entering place of worship

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letters of the two words before it
entering means going inside, so the on word goes into the place of worship

parts.note: a mosque is a Muslim place of worship
RE means on, in the sense of concerning

explanation.surface: Unsuitably lively music being played in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes the opening letters; 'entering' gives MORESQUE. 'on' as RE is the crossword sense of concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: A humoresque is a short, lively and playful piece of instrumental music.

clue.text: Abandons game having nothing to lose

indicators.note: to lose means to drop, so a letter is taken out of the game

parts.note: quoits is a game of throwing rings over a peg
O is the round figure meaning nothing

explanation.surface: Someone gives up a game when there is nothing left to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' drops O from QUOITS. Quoits is a ring-tossing game played at British fairs and on ships.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon something is to give it up or leave, which is to quit it.

clue.text: Allot food as announced

indicators.note: as announced means as spoken out, so the food word is given by its sound

parts.note: meat is food

explanation.surface: Handing out food, as the notice says.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to share out or distribute, which is to allot.

clue.text: Rubbish crew closed road in foreign city

parts.note: rot is rubbish or nonsense

indicators.note: closed means shut round, so the crew enclose the road

parts.note: a team is a crew

explanation.surface: Bin men close a road in a foreign city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closed' gives TERDAM: the crew close in around the road. 'Rubbish crew' looks like bin men but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a major Dutch port, so a city abroad for a British setter.

clue.text: Tree that is shown by river on one sort of map

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the map letters come first

parts.note: OS is Ordnance Survey, Britain's official mapping agency
IE is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A tree shown beside a river on a particular kind of map.
explanation.walkthrough: Ordnance Survey maps are the standard British maps for walkers.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a willow, a tree whose shoots are used for basket-making.

clue.text: Tacky pile fixed by Canadian family taking only one year

indicators.note: fixed by means held in place by, so the Canadian piece holds the pile inside it

parts.note: CAN is the abbreviation for Canadian
a heap is a pile

indicators.note: taking only one means keeping a single one, so one of the two year letters goes

parts.note: a dynasty is a ruling family

explanation.surface: A tacky pile put up by a Canadian family in just one year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed by' puts the pile in the Canadian piece; 'taking only one' leaves DNASTY, since the family has two year letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean cheaply made and in poor taste, the sense of shoddy.
